issues.claim: §4.3 *Raised ways* (l. 5124–5128) says a raised way's 'deck, supports, feet, spans and an aqueduct's channel live in their own arena part of the ground layer … its supports are footprints on its part'. That contradicts the owner's rule (g item 110 (b): 'Its piers are footprints on the ground part'), §2.7's `RaisedWayRecord.supports.ring` ('its footprint on ground part 0'), §3.4's raised-ways bullet ('its piers are footprints on part 0 … which part-0 stages read through the services') and its two feet ('each a vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part'), and V05 §1 / V04 (piers on ground part 0). Arena isolation (§3.10) and every part-0 reader of the piers depend on which arena holds them.
issues.required_change: §4.3 *Raised ways*: replace 'its deck, supports, feet, spans and an aqueduct's channel live in their own arena part of the ground layer' with 'its deck, spans and an aqueduct's channel live in their own arena part of the ground layer', and 'its supports are footprints on its part' with 'its supports are footprints on ground part 0 (§2.7's `supports`) and each of its two feet a vertex on part 0 joined by record to one on its part (§3.4)'.

issues.claim: g item 110 (b)'s raised ground parts are absent from the model's arena definitions the kernel cites: §2.2's `PlatKey` comment (l. 543) lists 'part 0 = the ground …; underground parts ≥ 1 …; sky parts ≥ 1 …' and no ground part ≥ 1; §2.1's *Arena parts* bullet (l. 516–522) names the ground, the underground parts and the sky parts and only the counters `nextUndergroundPart` and `nextSkyPart`, though §2.9 declares `nextGroundPart` (l. 2745) and §2.4/§2.7 say a raised way lies 'on a ground arena part ≥ 1 (§2.1)'; §2.2 rule 1's 'other arenas take the same five views' list gives no level mapping (L0–L4) for a raised part; rule 2's list of arenas that never share topology and of cross-arena links omits raised parts and their feet. The kernel's §3.4 ('as the underground's and the sky's parts are (§2.2's `PlatKey`)'), §3.2 (9) (a raised part's outer ring 'the frame with its margin (§2.2 rule 1 …)'), §3.7 (a raised part's bands) and §3.10 (arena isolation) therefore point at text that does not state the fact (the kernel's cross-part notes 3–4 not closed).
issues.required_change: §2.2 `PlatKey` comment: add 'ground parts ≥ 1 = one arena per raised way (g item 110 (b); §3.4), numbered by `Document.nextGroundPart`'. §2.1 *Arena parts*: add the raised ground parts to the list and `Document.nextGroundPart` to the counters that never decrease. §2.2 rule 1, *The other arenas*: add a bullet '**A raised ground part** (g item 110 (b)): L0 its outer ring — the ground's frame plus its context margin, growing with it by §3.2 (9) (§2.7 *At the frame*), a chain carrying `margin` on the raised way's record — and the one face inside it; L1 the raised way's centreline (a `way` chain); L2 its corridor band from `corridorUnion` (§3.7); L3–L4 none (a raised deck carries no plot, §2.7)'. §2.2 rule 2: 'The ground, each raised part of the ground layer, each underground part and each sky island are separate arenas …', and add 'a raised way's feet' to the cross-arena links.

issues.claim: A raised way's two feet are a one-ended hook. §3.4 says each foot is 'a vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part … Each end names its part (`{ part; at }`), so `resolve` reads it with that part's key'; §3.6's held set (3) holds 'a raised way's part-0 feet'; §3.10's stored-references row checks 'every indexed role … exactly one vertex … per ordinal (… a raised way's two feet each in the part its end names)'; §13.1 tests them. But `RaisedWayRecord` (§2.7, l. 2131–2140) has no feet field and §2.2 rule 7's vertex-role registry (l. 840) has no role for a foot (the underground link has `link_end`; nothing corresponds for raised feet), so no record stores the ends the kernel places, holds and checks (the kernel's cross-part note 5 not closed).
issues.required_change: §2.2 rule 7's vertex roles: add *`raised_foot`* (`('raised_foot', raised way id, 0 | 1)`: one vertex in ground part 0 and one in the raised way's part per foot, as `link_end`; g item 110 (b)). §2.7 `RaisedWayRecord`: add `feet: [{ part: number; at: VertexRef }, { part: number; at: VertexRef }]` per foot end (or state that the feet are the `raised_foot` rows, resolved per part), with the lifecycle sentence 're-placed by the raised way's re-derivation, one transaction per part (§3.4)'.

issues.claim: §3.4's raised-ways bullet says the parts are 'numbered from 1 …, allocated once and never renumbered or reused, as the underground's and the sky's parts are (§2.2's `PlatKey`)' without naming the counter (the model's cross-part note to the kernel, J-RM3: '§3.4 names `Document.nextGroundPart`'), and §3.2 (9)'s parenthesis sends a raised part's frame-with-margin outer ring to '§3.4', which does not state it — the statement is §2.7's *At the frame* (J-A110.22). The same bullet says the piers are 'footprints on part 0 (§2.7's `supports`), which part-0 stages read through the services', but a support's ring is a point attribute of the raised way's record (§2.7, §2.2 rule 5), which no kernel service (§3.4) returns; part-0 stages read it through §4.1's `raised` data key.
issues.required_change: §3.4 raised-ways bullet: 'numbered from 1 (part 0 is the ground) by `Document.nextGroundPart` (§2.9), allocated once …'. §3.2 (9): replace '— and each raised part of the ground layer, §3.4)' with '— and each raised part of the ground layer, §2.7 *At the frame*)'. §3.4 raised-ways bullet: 'its piers are footprints on part 0 (§2.7's `supports`), which part-0 stages read from the record through §4.1's `raised` data key'.

issues.claim: The mechanism W-FLD-01 added at §3.3 *Expectations* — a failed `KernelTx.expect` class floor returning `E_BELOW_MIN_WIDTH`/`_AREA`/`_ANGLE`, any other failed entry `E_INVARIANT`, and `onFail`'s three outcomes (`reject`: nothing committed, the code to the stage's class; `repair`: `absorbSliver` on each face below its floor, re-checked, rejected if a failure remains; `downgrade`: nothing committed, the code for the ladder's simpler rung) — has no test anywhere in §13 (no fixture names `expect`, `onFail` or a class floor failing inside a batch). Every mechanism that can fail needs its test (principles (7), (11)).
issues.required_change: §13.1's constructive set, after the §3.11 clause: 'a batch whose `expect` carries a class floor its result breaks, under each `onFail` — `reject` (version kept, the `E_BELOW_MIN_*` code returned), `repair` (a sliver below its width or area floor absorbed and the batch committed; a face below its angle floor still rejected after the repair), `downgrade` (version kept, the code returned) — and a failed non-floor entry (`E_INVARIANT`)'.

issues.claim: A stretch-state write (items 245, 575; §2.2 rule 5 *Stretch-state profiles*, *Write*, l. 806–808) places 'a knot at each end' of its `StretchRef`, but nothing states which ordinals the new knots take when the stretch lies between existing knots, nor that the profile is renumbered after the canonical form drops knots; §3.4's doors add a knot only with its ordinal ('any other indexed row carries its ordinal, an assertion otherwise') and §3.10's stored-references row requires 'every `ChainProfile`'s knots lie on its chain in ordinal order'. A mid-chain write therefore has no defined ordinal assignment, and the natural next-free ordinal fails §3.10 at save (`E_INVARIANT`). The kernel's cross-part note 6 asked for the renumbering; not applied (the river's control knots, by contrast, define theirs: `nextControl`, l. 921).
issues.required_change: §2.2 rule 5 *Stretch-state profiles*, *Write*: add 'After placing its end knots and applying the canonical form, the writer renumbers the profile's knots from 0 in chain order in the same batch — each knot row whose ordinal changes stripped by `removeEdges` on its `VertexRef` and re-added by `splitThrough` landing on its vertex with the new ordinal (§3.4's doors) — so §3.10's ordinal-order row holds; its undo record restores the former rows (as the profile's undo already does).'
